Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — it was helpful. A few follow-ups from our security and legal teams surfaced and I wanted to check Redwood's recommendations before we scope procurement:

1) Residency: we need to ensure all PHI (patient identifiers, notes) for EU clinics remain in EU jurisdiction — is Redwood's hosted API able to guarantee region-locked storage for logs, embeddings, and backups?

2) Retention windows: our retention policy is 90 days for raw transcripts, 1 year for de-identified summaries. What are common configurations within Redwood for retention limits and how do you enforce deletion/auditable erasure?

3) Redaction / pseudonymization: we expect to remove direct identifiers before storage but want details on on-the-fly redaction vs post-processing (and whether Redwood provides tools for deterministic pseudonymization or field-level masking).

4) Cache and model KV retention: does Redwood persist KV cache or prefixes beyond request lifetime for private deployments? If yes, how are those purged?

I've attached our security questionnaire and a simple data map. Can you route to the right folks and share a concise playbook (bullet list + playbook PDF) that we can present to legal? We're on a tight procurement timeline and would like any cost/operational tradeoffs up front.

Appreciate it — can we also get a 30-minute sync early next week?

Best,
Liam Turner

Wellbridge Health

Hi Liam — thanks for the detailed note and the attachments. Looping in Marcus (commercial) and Karthik (security/infra) who will help with cost and technical specifics. Below is a concise playbook you can share with legal — I'll follow up with an exported PDF and a proposed MAP (mutual action plan).

Quick answers + recommended configuration (high level):

- Residency guarantees: For hosted EU-region customers we provision compute and persistent storage in EU cloud regions only (data plane + audit logs). For strict jurisdictional needs we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which gives you customer-controlled KMS and an option for an air-gapped appliance.

- Retention model: Redwood supports retention policies per-tenant and per-route:
  * Raw request transcripts: configurable retention (min 0 days, default 30 days).
  * Embedding/KV cache: configurable time-to-live; recommended TTL = 24 hours for interactive sessions.
  * Derived artifacts (summaries, analytics): stored under "derived" bucket with separate retention (default 365 days).
  Enforcement: deletions are enacted via a bounded async job that marks objects for deletion and removes them from index + blob storage; deletions are recorded in the audit log (immutable append-only ledger) with timestamp and actor.

- Erasure/Right-to-be-forgotten: We provide tenant-scoped erasure APIs that accept identifiers or query predicates; the process returns a job id and final audit record. For regulated workflows we recommend a two-step flow: 1) soft-mark (prevent further access), 2) physical purge within the configured retention SLA (can be expedited under contract).

- Redaction & pseudonymization options:
  * On-the-fly redaction: Redwood can run a configurable redact pipeline (PII/PHI regex + model detectors) before any persistent write — recommended when you want to avoid storing direct identifiers at all.
  * Post-processing redaction: useful if you need raw transcripts in a short-lived buffer for QA; you must run the redact job within the retention window and mark originals for deletion.
  * Deterministic pseudonymization: supported via per-tenant salt and reversible token store (optional) — useful when you need consistent mapping across records.
  * Field-level masking: we support JSON-path based masks during ingestion (keep structure, mask values).

- KV cache: In the hosted flow the runtime keeps ephemeral KV caches in memory and a short-lived on-disk checkpoint (configurable TTL). Persistent KV caching across restarts requires Dedicated or Private deployments and can be set to auto-purge.

- Backups & snapshots: Backups are region-scoped and encrypted; retention for backups is independent. For strict policies we can include a backup retention floor in contract and limit cross-region replication.

Next steps and tradeoffs to highlight for legal/procurement:
  1) Hosted EU with tenant-scoped retention + on-the-fly redaction: fastest onboarding, lowest infra ops, reasonable for most regulated customers.
  2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with KMS-managed keys: predictable throughput and stronger isolation; allows stricter backup/retention SLAs.
  3) Private (VPC or on-prem appliance): maximum control over residency, KMS, and audit evidence — higher ops cost and longer lead time.

Requested artifacts I'll deliver by EOD tomorrow:
  - Concise playbook PDF summarizing the bullets above (incl. deletion API examples + SLA options)
  - Redaction algorithm summary (regex + model-based heuristics) and sample JSON-path masks
  - MAP with proposed dates for implementation and an expedited deletion SLA option (if needed)

Marcus/Karthik — can you add cost delta and any requirements we should push into contract? Liam — please share preferred times for a 30-min sync tomorrow or Tue morning CET.

Hi Liam — quick commercial note from our side:

- Baseline: Hosted EU with tenant retention controls and on-the-fly redaction has the fastest lead (2–3 business days) and minimal contract changes.
- Dedicated: +20–35% on unit costs depending on committed throughput; includes tighter backup policies and ability to set shorter purge SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time setup + annual platform fee and managed support; we can include an accelerated deletion SLA (48 hours) as a paid add-on.

I'll include a short cost appendix in the MAP and label the options with approximate MRR/commit targets tied to RW-8421.
